meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Unitary National Jurisdiction, no sub-state corporate tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code heritage with material EU-directive harmonization; unitary judicial and company registry system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Income and Capital Tax Treaty (1996, as amended by Protocols of 2004 and 2009)
Luxembourg–China (PRC) Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 16 March 2017)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (1967, as amended by 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (2012, with Protocol)
Benelux Economic Union Treaty (1944/1958, as consolidated)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment and free movement of capital, Arts. 49 and 63 TFEU)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (including the 2022 and 2023 AML/CFT reform waves); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 28 July 2023 implementing the legitimate-interest access regime following CJEU Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 23 December 2016 (introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale, Arts. 158-1 to 158-14); CSSF Regulation 12-02 and CSSF Circulars 18/698, 20/744 and 23/797; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 January 2019 (RBE filing mechanics); FIU (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) guidance.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (competent authorities, AML-obligated entities, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; no unrestricted public access after CJEU C-37/20 and C-601/20)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft articles of association (statuts) and partnership deed of the SCSp, including management powers of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (public deed is market standard; private deed permitted by law unless contributions include real estate rights)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) for signature pages executed abroad; domestic Luxembourg deed requires no apostille for RCS filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and constitutional deed of any corporate general partner (associé commandité)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry of the corporate general partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, or consular legalization for jurisdictions not party to the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified identity documents, proof of residential address, and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds declarations of ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Civil identity registry or public notary in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified French, German, or English translation attached

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letters and independent written authorization for the destination payment rails (Stripe/PayPal merchant KYC backstop)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originator bank or licensed payment institution of the financing partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the bank officer's signature or SWIFT-attested banker's letter where the receiving bank's KYC policy so permits

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) for incorporation agents and ultimate signatories executing the RCS filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Grantor before a notary or the consular section of a Luxembourg embassy in the grantor's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille, with consular legalization for non-1961-Convention states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing (not less than 12-monthly) screening of all UBOs, general partners, limited partners, authorized signatories and closely-related persons against: (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (including Regulations (EU) No 269/2014 and (EU) No 765/2006 as amended), (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists (ISIL/Al-Qaida 1267/1989, Taliban 1988, 1373), (iii) US OFAC SDN/SSI and Part 561 lists (relevant to USD-denominated Stripe/PayPal card rails), (iv) Luxembourg FIU strategic analysis files and the PEP definition of CSSF Circular 18/698, and (v) adverse-media and global watchlist databases. Enhanced due diligence is automatic upon any PEP identification, crypto-asset source of funds, or counterparty in a FATF high-risk third jurisdiction; positive hits trigger a mandatory suspicious-transaction report to the CRF under the Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, electronic filing via eJustice.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory texts and registry filings must be in French, German, or Luxembourgish; a certified French translation of the constitutional instrument is the notarial and registry standard. The SCSp name must appear in Latin script; non-Latin-script brand elements must be transliterated phonetically into the Latin alphabet. The mandatory legal-form suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' must follow the corporate name in all commercial, invoice and payment-rail communications, and the name must not mislead as to the nature or regulated status of the activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Banking (prior CSSF banking licence under Law of 5 April 1993 required)
Assurance, Insurance, Réassurance (prior Commissariat aux Assurances approval required)
Fonds, FCP, SICAV, OPC, UCITS (prior CSSF investment-fund authorisation required under Law of 17 December 2010)
Gestion de fortune, Wealth Management, SGP (CSSF regulated-activity licence required)
Fiduciaire, Trust, Trustee (regulated fiduciary activity requiring MIFA/CSSF registration)
Paiement, Payment Services, PSP (PSD2 licence under Law of 10 November 2009 required)
Bourse, Stock Exchange, Clearing House (CSSF licence required)
Red Cross, Croix-Rouge, humanitarian emblems (protected by Geneva Conventions and EU law)
État, Ministère, Administration, Commune, National (implied connection with public authorities, subject to ministry objection)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the notary or applicant (i) re-files a modified name on the LBR/eJustice portal, restarting the 30-day reservation clock at minimal tariff; (ii) files a written summary appeal (recours) before the President of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de et à Luxembourg within 1 month of the refusal, requesting revocation of the registry's negative decision; (iii) for prior-ministerial-approval tokens, re-submits the draft name through the notary to the competent ministry (Ministry of Finance for banking tokens, Ministry of Justice for fiduciary tokens) - ministerial silence is never deemed consent and refusal is challengeable by administrative recours within 3 months; (iv) may request one renewal of the reservation for an additional 30 days upon written justification filed before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The SCSp must maintain a registered office physically located in Luxembourg at a material address; a mailbox-only virtual office is tolerated by the RCS only where the general partner and a local administrator confirm that (i) statutory books, the UBO file, accounting records and general-partner resolutions are physically available at that address, and (ii) official correspondence is reviewed within 5 business days. For a POD apparel retail entity collecting payments via Stripe/PayPal, Luxembourg FIU and CSSF substance expectations require genuine local administration commensurate with activity; a purely virtual address materially increases onboarding refusal risk at Luxembourg payment service providers and correspondent banks.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 5-10% probability within the first 12 months of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the RCS, Luxembourg FIU, or CSSF-appointed auditors for a Low_Risk_Standard POD retail SCSp; probability rises to 15-25% if PEP or sanctions hits are flagged, annual card volume exceeds EUR 3 million, or a nominee general partner participates.

Notarization of the SCSp constitutive deed and partnership deed before a Luxembourg notary

Statutory zero-fee filing; preparation included in advising counsel's incorporation package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market translator tariff (EUR 0.22-0.45 per word for an average due-diligence file)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization of up to six foreign-issued corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (Luxembourg consular section) or competent consulate of the document's country of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg licensed service provider (PSF, trust company or fiduciary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a standard SCSp registered-office and administrative-services arrangement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for preparation of a dual-rail merchant KYC file covering class-2 customs retail and POD goods

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 16-1 to 16-6 (special limited partnership provisions); Law of 11 July 2013 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration de constitution (Declaration of Incorporation) together with the Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société en Commandite Spéciale)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required by law; no escrow account or notarized bank certificate is required for a Special Limited Partnership (SCSp)
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner and the initial Limited Partner approve the formation of the SCSp, subscribe to all partnership interests, and accept the stated capital contribution without requirement of minimum capital. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is adopted at [Registered Address] in Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed as Manager and Authorised Signatory, with authority to open banking accounts, execute payment contracts, and submit registrations. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all acts already taken to effect incorporation and any permitted licensing are hereby ratified. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners acting by private deed or, if real property contributions are made, by a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the SCSp partnership agreement in writing, stipulating the legal form, corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, identities and contributions of the General Partner and Limited Partner(s), profit-sharing arrangement, management powers, and liquidation rights. If contributions include real estate or registered assets, a notarial deed is required. Sign all pages and ensure each partner's signature is authenticated, either directly or by a duly authorised attorney-in-fact.
required_dossiers: Certified identification documents (passport/ID) of all partners
Power of attorney if signed by a representative
Proof of registered office acceptance from the Luxembourg fiduciary or service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is rejected or queried for incompleteness, amend the offending clauses, have all parties re-execute the corrected version, and re-submit the full package with any missing supporting documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – online portal at www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS registration application using the official electronic form (form B). Attach the executed partnership agreement together with the declaration of constitution. Provide full details of the General Partner, Limited Partner(s), managers, registered office address, and the SCSp's designated activity code. Pay the applicable filing fee. Upon approval, the RCS issues a Registration Certificate and a permanent RCS identification number.
required_dossiers: Statement of registered office acceptance from the legal owner/landlord or service provider
Identity documents of the manager(s) and partners
Proof of payment of the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS files an opposition or query, respond in writing within the prescribed deadline (typically 1-3 months), provide clarifications or corrected attachments, and request that the application be re-examined. If still rejected, file a formal appeal with the district court within 15 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Publication in the Electronic Compilation of Companies (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – RESA publication service (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file the legally required notice with RESA for publication of the SCSp's incorporation details, including its name, registered office, date of the partnership agreement, notary if applicable, and the identities of the General Partner and authorised manager(s). Ensure publication is completed within one month of the RCS registration date.
required_dossiers: Copy of the RCS Registration Certificate
Extract of the partnership agreement containing all legally required particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published notice contains errors, immediately file a voluntary corrective notice with RESA and, if third parties have relied on the incorrect information, coordinate with the RCS to ensure the public register reflects the accurate details without prejudice to third parties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Value Added Tax and Social Security Registrations (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – VAT Department; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp for Luxembourg VAT if it engages in taxable transactions in Luxembourg or crosses the annual VAT threshold (EUR 35,000 for e-commerce supplies). Submit Form 1 (VAT registration) to the ACD, indicating the activity of online retail of custom print-on-demand merchandise. If the SCSp will hire employees, register the partners/employees with the CCSS for social security. No municipal business tax registration is needed if the SCSp has no physical business premises in Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: RCS Registration Certificate and RCS number
Passport copies of the General Partner and tax representative (if any)
CMS banking details if VAT refunds are anticipated
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT registration is delayed or rejected, request retroactive registration by explaining the delay and submitting a fully completed form. If the CCSS requires physical business premises, clarify that the SCSp is an online e-commerce business and no local hiring has occurred, or provide a plan for social security registration once employees are engaged.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no industrial licensing authority applies to a purely remote print-on-demand retail trade
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no statutory operating licence or manufacturing permit is required for POD custom apparel retailing

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – category not triggered for online retail activity with no on-site printing, dyeing, or manufacturing processes
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste thresholds are imposed for a purely commercial retail operation. If the SCSp later establishes a physical printing workshop, it will be subject to the EU Industrial Emissions Directive and Luxembourg's classed establishments regulations, requiring prior environmental authorisation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required – no physical store, warehouse, or production workshop is maintained. If the SCSp operates from a home office, general fire safety and workplace health rules under the Luxembourg Labour Code apply; no separate civil defence or municipal clearance is necessary.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct tax registration; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT registration and indirect tax administration; Luxembourg Tax Administration portal: guichet.lu / myguichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity or a Luxembourg SCSp acting as a taxable person for VAT must file a VAT registration application with the AEDT on form 010 (Formulaire de demande d'immatriculation à la TVA). The application requires identification of the partnership, its authorized representative, actual economic activity, estimated turnover, and any non-EU entity's local tax representative if established outside the EU/EEA. In the case of an SCSp without legal personality, the registration is made in the name of the partnership itself when the partnership has a fixed establishment in Luxembourg or, if the SCSp has no Luxembourg establishment, in the name of its statutory manager/representative for VAT. The Luxembourg business number (matricule) issued by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) is required before or concurrently with the VAT registration. After validation, the AEDT issues a Luxembourg national identification number for VAT (numéro d'identification à la TVA) bearing the 'LU' prefix. A non-EU principal with no permanent establishment in Luxembourg may appoint an individual tax representative approved by the AEDT, who is jointly and severally liable for the VAT obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. A Luxembourg SCSp (Société en commandite spéciale) is a special limited partnership without legal personality and is fiscally transparent by default. For Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax purposes, the SCSp is generally not itself a taxpayer; its profits and deductions flow through to its general and limited partners in proportion to their entitlement, and each partner is taxed in their own jurisdiction on their allocable share. For VAT purposes, the SCSp is nevertheless treated as a taxable person where it independently carries out an economic activity, and the partnership itself registers and remits VAT in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No direct check-the-box election equivalent to the U.S. entity classification election exists under Luxembourg law. The fiscal transparency of an SCSp is the default statutory treatment and is not elective. Certain Luxembourg partnerships may, upon meeting specific legal conditions, opt for corporate income tax treatment only if they are transformed into a corporate vehicle (e.g., a société à responsabilité limitée or société anonyme) by a notarial deed, which is a civil-law conversion, not a tax classification election. Luxembourg has also enacted anti-hybrid rules consistent with ATAD (EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive) that may recharacterize a transparent entity where a foreign jurisdiction treats the same entity as opaque, and hybrid mismatch election mechanisms generally restrict rather than grant preferential pass-through status. No elective transparency regime exists for SCSp beyond the statutory default.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual taxable turnover excluding VAT) for small-enterprise exemption from Luxembourg VAT; mandatory VAT registration is required once taxable supplies of goods or services exceed this threshold in the course of an economic activity, subject to special EU distance-sales thresholds and non-established supplier rules. E-commerce marketplace and distance-sales threshold: EUR 10,000 for cross-border intra-Community distance sales of goods to Luxembourg consumers before the EU-wide EUR 10,000 common threshold applies under the OSS (One Stop Shop) regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time continuous transaction control (CTC) system or mandatory digital fiscal stamping applies to B2B or B2C e-commerce invoicing in Luxembourg. Electronic invoicing is permitted and legally equivalent to paper invoices, subject to authenticity of origin and integrity of content via advanced electronic signature, EDI, or reliable audit trail. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only in the B2G (business-to-government) segment: suppliers to Luxembourg public-sector entities must issue electronic invoices through the Peppol network and the Luxembourg national Peppol Authority (SIGI), unless exception applies. For POD apparel e-commerce, no specific API-based fiscal clearance or electronic invoice authorization step is required under Luxembourg domestic law, but records must be retained and made available to the AEDT in case of audit. OSS (One Stop Shop) registration via Luxembourg's portal is mandatory for certain cross-border supplies to consumers to simplify EU VAT compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A POD apparel seller may apply the Luxembourg 0% VAT rate to supplies of goods physically exported by the seller or on its behalf to a destination outside the European Union. Zero-rating applies where: (i) the goods are dispatched or transported out of Luxembourg to a non-EU country; (ii) the export is evidenced by an accepted customs export declaration; (iii) the exporter is the owner or has the power of disposal over the goods at the time of dispatch; (iv) the goods leave the EU within the statutory period (generally 90 days from dispatch; extension may apply); and (v) the supplier retains complete documentary proof of export. Zero-rating also applies to directly related services, transport, and freight forwarders associated with exported goods. If the POD apparel is supplied to a customer in another EU Member State and transported by the customer, intra-Community supply exemption (0%) applies only where the customer's VAT ID and a correct EC Sales List are in place. For e-commerce sales of low-value goods to non-EU consumers, Luxembourg zero-rating is available where export transport conditions are met and the supplier keeps the required evidence in its accounting records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DAU) accepted by Luxembourg or another EU customs office
Commercial invoice issued by the Luxembourg seller or the SCSp to the non-EU buyer
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing physical departure from the EU
Proof of dispatch from Luxembourg including carrier tracking and customs movement reference number (MRN)
Inward remittance certificate or bank transfer/payment processor confirmation evidencing consideration received from the non-EU purchaser
Order and contract documentation identifying the buyer, goods, and sale terms (e.g., collection of AMD/other payment records for POD transactions)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT audits export zero-rating claims strictly. If documentation is not produced or proves insufficient, the export is not accepted as zero-rated, and the full Luxembourg VAT becomes due from the seller, with late payment interest and potential penalties. Wrongful zero-rating or fraudulent claims may result in: (i) reassessment of VAT on the supply at 17%; (ii) late-payment interest; (iii) administrative fines of up to EUR 10,000 per infringement depending on gravity; (iv) criminal penalties for tax fraud under the Luxembourg General Tax Law, including imprisonment in aggravated cases; and (v) joint and several liability of the legal representative or local tax representative. The statute of limitations for reassessment is generally five years for domestic transactions and up to ten years in case of fraud. Repeated clawbacks also trigger enhanced scrutiny for subsequent export claims, and a POD operator must maintain complete transactional evidence for at least ten years to satisfy Luxembourg and EU record-keeping requirements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem/ESCB framework and in regulatory coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for payment services, AML/CFT supervision, and banking licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility applies to both current-account and capital-account transactions by virtue of Luxembourg's euro-area membership and Articles 63-65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no Luxembourg domestic exchange controls, no territorial restrictions on the disposition of export proceeds, and no prior authorisation requirements for profit remittance, partner distributions, or dividend-equivalent transfers from an SCSp to non-resident partners. EU restrictive measures (sanctions) and CSSF/BCL AML-CFT screening are the only practical constraints. For a POD retail SCSp settling via Stripe/PayPal, foreign-currency balances (USD, GBP, CHF) may be freely held, converted, or swept to EUR without BCL licences; only ordinary statistical balance-of-payments reporting is collected through resident credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation exists in Luxembourg. Export proceeds from non-EU print-on-demand sales need not be repatriated, converted to EUR, or held with a Luxembourg-resident bank. There are no mandatory conversion ratios, no repatriation time limits, and no BCL notification deadlines for individual exporters. Receipts may remain in USD/GBP on Stripe/PayPal accounts or in dedicated multi-currency accounts until operational outflows occur. The receiving Luxembourg bank applies the standard BCL external position statistical classification (direct investment/trade in goods) but imposes no treasury restriction.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (compte à vue) with multi-currency sub-ledgers; optional Capital Escrow Account for partner contributions

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess/BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Business Account and SEPA Clearing Account
Operational Account / E-commerce Aggregator Settlement Account
Operational Account for SME and partnership structures

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium-High for EU/EEA-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passported into Luxembourg or directly licensed by the CSSF. Target rails are fully viable: PayPal (Luxembourg) S.à r.l. holding a CSSF EMI licence, and Stripe operating in the EU through Stripe Technology Europe Ltd (Central Bank of Ireland licence, passported to Luxembourg under PSD2/EMD2). These EMIs may settle in EUR and provide connected bank accounts through partner credit institutions holding BCL/CSSF licences. Offshore (non-EEA) EMIs are rated Low-to-Non-viable due to the CSSF passporting requirement under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 (AML/CFT) and the Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services; cross-border acceptance of unauthorised non-EEA EMIs is a regulatory breach. A POD SCSp should maintain a primary EUR account at a tier-1 Luxembourg bank receiving Stripe/PayPal payouts to avoid PSP concentration risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for one authorised signatory of the general partner (SCSp managing partner or the corporate GP's statutory director). Under CSSF Circular EMF-2012-001 and the Law of 12 November 2004, Luxembourg credit institutions must identify the business relationship principal and beneficial owner. Video identification is accepted only under CSSF-approved remote KYC systems or via a notarised deed/certified ID copy. For the SCSp structure, the GP company and each limited partner owning 10% or more must undergo individual KYC; remote opening is technically available for silent partners with certified passport copies, but in practice a first in-person visit to the bank or to a Luxembourg notary is required. Recommended approach: schedule a physical onboarding at BCEE or BGL BNP Paribas, attend with the GP director, and present the complete partnership dossier plus substance evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through SCSp opacity: multi-layer partners, foreign ownership above 50%, and no minimum capital interpreted as a shell/fund risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société) with a partner schedule; 2) Luxembourg beneficial owner register (RBE/Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) filing receipt; 3) individual UBO forms identifying all natural persons and percentage ownership; 4) group structure chart and commercial substance report signed by the statutory auditor; 5) tax pass-through confirmation from the Luxembourg tax administration where requested; 6) opening balance sheet and certified capital contribution bank proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity e-commerce cross-border settlement via PSP aggregators (Stripe/PayPal), CNP card-present fraud red flags, and refund mismatch anomalies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Signed Stripe Connected Account and PayPal Business agreements; 2) verified domain/property title and active storefront URL showing live POD merchandising; 3) 12-month PSP-to-bank transaction flow ledger mapping settlement IDs to invoices and orders; 4) documented refund, chargeback, and dispute resolution policy; 5) export customs evidence (CN22/CN23) for non-EU shipments; 6) completed AML onboarding questionnaire listing expected transaction values, counterparty geographies, and merchandise categories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ISIC 4791 requires no statutory licence; banks may classify low-capital e-commerce ventures as high-turnover shell hybrids
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 1) Capital contribution bank credits showing committed working capital of at least EUR 50,000; 2) signed supply/fulfilment contract with a POD print operator across EU, UK, and US markets; 3) RCS (Luxembourg trade register) current status certificate and non-liquidation evidence; 4) certified profit forecast for three fiscal years with gross margin and platform fee schedules; 5) agreement evidencing local administrative substance, such as domiciliation agent, registered office, or part-time local compliance manager.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 from each subscribing partner's bank into the SCSp EUR IBAN (LUxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx) with remittance field 70 reading 'SCSp capital contribution — [date], [partner legal name], [subscription deed ref.]'. Non-EU inbound USD/GBP transfers must be accompanied by a source-of-funds certificate; the receiving Luxembourg bank applies BCL balance-of-payments classification code F.51 (inward direct investment, equity participation) with no BCL authorisation step. Verification protocol: (i) GP/board resolution accepting the contribution; (ii) updated RBE filing if ownership changes; (iii) capital confirmation letter countersigned by the statutory auditor. Inbound currency conversion may be executed at a preferential treasury rate or parked in a USD sub-account pending operational outlay. Cash contributions require no notarisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: 1) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT / SCT-Instant) for EU-based print shops, warehouses, and ad-tech vendors, in EUR with no charge and settlement within 20 seconds; 2) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for non-EU garment and blank-wholesale suppliers in Asia and the US, using USD/EUR multi-currency sweep accounts; 3) Commercial irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit for batch procurements exceeding EUR 50,000 to vendors in non-OECD jurisdictions, confirmed by a top-20 EU bank where the beneficiary demands; 4) regular payout sweeps from Stripe/PayPal to the SCSp settlement account on a T+2 or T+3 basis to reduce PSP float concentration and platform bankruptcy risk; 5) partner distributions executed as clearly labelled SEPA or MT103 payments with remittance text 'Distribution — FY [year]', matched against certified distributable profit to avoid lender clawback or AML misclassification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable vanilla forward contracts with tenor up to 12 months transacted with BGL BNP Paribas, BCEE, or BIL under an ISDA or 2018 EU Master Agreement where available; no mandatory clearing as the SCSp is a small non-financial counterparty
EUR/GBP vanilla deliverable forward for UK settlement exposure arising from PayPal GBP floats, capped at 80% of forecast 90-day sales
Vanilla EUR/USD FX swaps used exclusively for working capital duration realignment, tenors below 6 months, with mark-to-market collaterisation only at bank discretion

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only if the SCSp obtains genuine invoicing exposure in a non-convertible currency; for POD operations in USD, GBP, or CHF they are neither required nor recommended
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps limited to 24-month tenors where a committed purchase pipeline exceeding EUR 2,000,000 is evidenced by signed supply contracts
Zero-premium EUR/USD collar structures to neutralise platform settlement-date conversion uncertainty; strictly non-leveraged with no speculative FX options

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements filing with RCS (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 5,000 after formal notice; prolonged non-compliance may result in judicial strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners in the RBE (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once each calendar year; confirmation filed online via eJustice by 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 1,250 and up to 6 months imprisonment for liable managers; repeated non-compliance may lead to court-ordered enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Update of RCS/RBE records upon changes in partners, managers, registered office, or partnership agreement amendments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS and RBE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the relevant corporate change; no separate filing is required for no-change years.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 10,000 for late RCS filings; RBE update failures are subject to fines up to EUR 1,250 plus potential administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (if the SCSp is registered under the simplified annual VAT scheme)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 April of the following calendar year for the annual return; monthly/quarterly returns have separate statutory deadlines.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 10% of the VAT due; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; ex officio assessment after prolonged default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit becomes mandatory if the SCSp exceeds at least two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total over EUR 4.4 million; net turnover over EUR 8.8 million; average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Small enterprises are exempt; audit may also be required by the partnership agreement or by an applicable regulated-fund regime.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; consolidated accounts may be prepared under IFRS; registered SCSp annual accounts must be filed with the RCS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must confirm the accuracy of the RBE beneficial-owner data at least once per calendar year through the eJustice portal. Any transfer of partnership interests that affects beneficial ownership must be reported within 1 month; the annual confirmation thereafter reflects the updated register.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of partners / members (registre des associés)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate effective rate in Luxembourg City (CIT 17% + solidarity/unemployment surcharge of 7% on CIT + Municipal Business Tax 6.75%). The SCSp is fiscally transparent: no CIT at entity level; each partner is taxed on its distributive share (resident corporate partner aggregate about 24.94%; resident individual partner progressive up to 42% plus solidarity surcharge).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full pass-through eliminates entity-level tax leakage; profit distributions to partners are withdrawals, not dividends. The SCSp remains subject to Municipal Business Tax (6.75% Luxembourg City) because POD retail qualifies as a commercial undertaking. Investment tax credit: 8% of the first EUR 150,000 of qualifying software/POD automation capex and 6% above the threshold, claimable by partners through their distributive share. Losses flow through and may be used by partners under their own regimes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 520 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités / partnership assessment declaration) filed via the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD) e-filing portal MyGuichet.lu / eCDF by the appointed general partner (gérant) or its registered Luxembourg tax representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end for self-filing; extended to 31 December of that year where filing is made by a registered Luxembourg tax adviser (OEC/ACD-registered representative).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg fiscal registration number, legal form code SCSp, RCS registration number, registered seat and registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp files as a Luxembourg taxpayer even though CIT falls on partners; identify each non-resident partner with foreign TIN and country of tax residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable commercial profit; reconciliation of statutory accounts to tax result: depreciation, add-backs, exempt income, and digital/e-commerce expenses (POD platform fees, print costs, Stripe/PayPal merchant charges, logistics).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare in EUR; maintain transfer pricing documentation for related print/fulfilment suppliers under LIR art. 56 to support cross-border cost allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the annual tax result per partner: general partner(s) and limited partner(s), percentage shares, capital accounts and current-account adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partner shares are separately assessed by the ACD; the SCSp must disclose foreign partners on demand to avoid penalty assessment; no withholding tax applies to distributive shares.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Ex-officio (estimated) assessment by the ACD; 10%-15% additional tax surcharge for late or incorrect declarations; late-payment interest 0.6% per month on arrears; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 for refusal to produce accounting records; criminal prosecution for deliberate concealment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 610 (Déclaration de l'impôt commercial communal - Municipal Business Tax) filed via ACD/MyGuichet by the SCSp as a commercial undertaking carrying on POD retail.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same statutory block as Form 520 (31 May self-filing; 31 December with a registered professional agent); prepayments assessed by the commune of the registered seat.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trade profit as determined for CIT before application of the Municipal Business Tax abatement and commercial-tax-specific allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp is liable for Municipal Business Tax even where all partners are non-resident; the partnership-level abatement is restricted where partners are non-resident individual traders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory add-backs (e.g., 50% of certain management fees, 25% of long-term debt interest) and allocation of the tax base to the relevant commune (Luxembourg City rate 6.75%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No reduction for a registered office in Luxembourg City; only actual premises/activity factors may reduce the allocable base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same enforcement regime as CIT: 10%-15% surcharge, 0.6% monthly interest, estimation by the commune, and personal/general-partner joint liability for unpaid prepayments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax on distributions of Luxembourg resident capital companies (SA, Sàrl). An SCSp is fiscally transparent; distributions of profits to partners are capital/current-account withdrawals and attract NO dividend withholding tax at partnership level. The 15% rate can apply where the SCSp or an underlying holding company pays dividends to a partner in a non-participation context.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since SCSp distributions normally carry no Luxembourg WHT, treaty relief is primarily invoked at the partner's residence under the applicable DTA partnership article. Where WHT does arise on dividends from underlying Luxembourg companies held by the SCSp, the recipient must: (i) prove beneficial ownership; (ii) hold a foreign residence certificate (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority; (iii) submit the Luxembourg reduced-WHT form (demande de remboursement / décharge) to the ACD with shareholding and holding-period evidence; (iv) claim EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 0% rate for qualifying holdings of at least 10% held for 12 months, or DTA rates typically 5% (substantial holding) and 15% (portfolio).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes NO withholding tax on outbound interest or royalties to non-residents. Exceptions: (i) 20% final WHT on certain interest paid to resident individuals in a private/savings capacity; (ii) thin-capitalisation or profit-participating debt recharacterised as hidden dividend distributions subject to 15% dividend WHT; (iii) abusive arrangements denied treaty and EU Directive benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 group consolidated revenue triggers Luxembourg Master File and Local File obligations under the Law of 18 December 2015 and Circular LIR 56/1 - 57/3 - 164/2; Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000. A standalone SCSp POD retailer normally falls below the thresholds, but contemporaneous TP documentation must still be kept where related-party print or fulfilment services are purchased.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Circular LIR n. 14/4 (28 January 2022) denies treaty benefits and tax-residence certification to letterbox entities lacking minimum substance: local premises, personnel, local bank account, management meetings in Luxembourg, and complete accounting records. The SCSp exercising genuine POD activity (online store, merchant accounts, print-supplier contracts, inventory turnover) has inherent substance, but the general partner must evidence governance by holding partner/management meetings in Luxembourg and maintaining statutory books and beneficiary registers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Declaration (Luxembourg Abgabenordnung Arts. 55, 57, 396)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting POD revenues, diverting sales through private PayPal/Stripe accounts, fabricating print-supplier invoices, or persistently filing nil returns while the business generates taxable turnover.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10-15% administrative surcharge plus 0.6% monthly late interest; criminal tax fraud: fine up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years; aggravated or systematic schemes may trigger higher fines and forfeiture of the illicit profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner (gérant) is jointly and severally liable for the SCSp's tax debts where the structure is a sham or assets have been stripped; the ACD can pierce the veil, issue travel bans, attach personal assets, and prosecute de facto managers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Letterbox Company / Substance Failure (Circular LIR n. 14/4)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining only a registered-agent address with no real management, no local bank account, and all decisions taken abroad, while claiming Luxembourg tax residence; or using an SCSp as a conduit for related-party e-commerce profits without commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the structure; denial of tax-residence certificate and treaty benefits; profit reallocation to the foreign beneficial owner; additional assessment at statutory rates plus penalties and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and de facto directors face civil restitution for dissipated corporate benefits, joint liability for the tax differential, and potential disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/KYC Failures of the Merchant Entity (Law of 12 November 2004 as amended; FATF standards)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the POD store without identifying beneficial owners, using anonymous or high-risk payment patterns through Stripe/PayPal, failing to register the economic ownership declaration (RBE), or not reporting suspicious transactions to the Luxembourg FIU (CRF).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for supervised professionals; freezing of merchant PSP accounts by the FIU; criminal sanctions for laundering the proceeds of tax evasion of up to 5 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for dissipated stored client funds; travel restrictions and imprisonment for principals in AML-linked fraud; accessory penalties may include prohibition from managing commercial companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border E-Commerce VAT / OSS Violations (Luxembourg Law of 19 February 2021; EU VAT E-Commerce Package)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report intra-EU distance sales through the Luxembourg One-Stop-Shop (OSS) portal, exceeding the EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold without registration, or failing to apply deemed-supplier rules when selling through online marketplaces to EU B2C customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment on all undeclared sales; 10% penalty plus 0.8% monthly default interest; exposure to tax audits in member states of consumption through the EU VAT Exchange; joint liability for VAT of non-EU print suppliers under certain supply-chain flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant is jointly liable for the SCSp's VAT debts where the partnership is left without assets or the declaration is knowingly void; travel bans can be imposed in enforcement proceedings for repeated VAT evasion.
